I have been using one sec for about a year or two now, and I originally used it primarily for the main “Take a deep breath” to give myself an unskippable cutscene before opening Instagram and YouTube. It works really well and it’s definitely annoying but that’s the point and it has assuredly helped break a lot of my brainrot cycles.

I’m giving it a review now because I recently started also using the app blocking feature, which allows you to set up a schedule such that certain apps can be blocked at certain times. I used to run late every morning because I would just doomscroll for way too long after waking up, but I set up a schedule to block all social media and games on my phone in the morning hours. It works really well and you can also set it up so that it’s literally impossible to turn off while it’s active, which is a feature I needed. 

The app offers a paid subscription for $19.99 a year with lots of other cool features, but the best part is that the features I just described are completely free! It’s helped me immensely in not getting lost in the sauce on my phone and I am very grateful.

title.label: Great option if you’re addicted to social media but too addicted to delete it yet!

content.label:
To be honest, I’m not really sure why I downloaded this app. I don’t even have social media. I thought perhaps it could aid me with keeping off of my YouTube app, which it did— only for me to watch YouTube on my TV instead LOL. 

I can see this being a good app for people who do have social media and need guilt-tripped into not doomscrolling. For me, this app just made me realize that I’m addicted to YouTube so I ordered about 20 books and will be deleting YouTube from my phone when they arrive. I think the “time saved” part of the app is inaccurate because I always spend more than 5 minutes on YouTube. I think I’d like to see some type of more realistic “summary” feature in this app. So at the end of the week when I get my screen time report from Apple I also get a notification from this app saying how much time I actually saved myself based on how long I usually spend on apps. 

Overall, though, this is super creative and the most effective way I’ve seen so far at keeping people from wasting time on their social media. The setup is confusing though, even for a young adult like me. Don’t think that can be worked around unfortunately. 

If I didn’t have the self-control that I already have not to have social media in the first place, I would definitely keep this app and pay for the subscription. I will likely be recommending it to people who ask for tips to stay off their phone.
